page.title: Cooking
page.purpose: Guide one cooking session a step at a time — full instruction, quantities, and timers — with explicit step completion, timers that survive reloads and other tabs, and a finish that keeps cooking separate from eating.

priorities.statement: The current step's title, full instruction, and needed quantities dominate and read from arm's length.
Next and Previous only move between steps; Mark step done is a separate explicit action.
Running timers stay visible with their state and survive leaving the screen, reloading, and other tabs.
Exit cooking is always visible and never cancels timers or records intake.
Finishing offers batch confirmation, I ate a serving, or finishing without bookkeeping as separate choices.
Dependency hints say what can happen while something else cooks, without trapping the reader on one step.

states.description: An active session showing the current step with the step list on desktop.
First read of the page's data; stable skeletons reserve the layout so nothing shifts on arrival, and no sample food is shown as saved data.
A write is in flight; the affected control shows a busy state and says why it is unavailable, and success appears only after the durable save.
The request failed; the reason and the next action are stated, pending edits are kept, and nothing is edited against a fake empty account.
The API is unreachable; the loaded recipe stays readable and timer controls persist locally for reconciliation.
The session's recipe has no method steps; the page says so and offers View meal or Edit instead of an empty timer screen.
Some step quantities or durations are unknown; they read Amount not set or Time not set, never zero, and no duration is invented.
Timer or completion state from another tab or device is newer than this view; it reconciles to the server revision and shows the latest state.
A matching active session exists; Resume and Start another are offered.
The current step is recorded done through Mark step done; its check comes from the persisted completion.
Marking a step done before its prerequisites are confirmed warns and offers an explicit override.
A step timer is running from an absolute deadline.
A timer is paused with its remaining duration.
A timer reached zero; it is marked elapsed, the step is not completed, and the expiry is acknowledged once.
Several timers run; the ones not on this step sit in a compact tray.
On phones the step list opens as a sheet without losing the current step.
The recipe was edited during the session; the session stays pinned and the new revision is offered explicitly.
The step has no image or the screen is short; instructions, quantities, and timers keep their priority.
The finish flow offers Confirm batch, I ate a serving, and Finish without inventory update.

claims.statement: Focused cooking hides the five-destination navigation while keeping Exit cooking obvious.
Exit cooking is visible without scrolling at every viewport and state.
On phones the step title, Mark step done, and Next step are reachable without scrolling; the step image gives way first.
Next step is the filled primary footer action; Previous step is secondary.
Moving between steps never changes completion; a step is done only through Mark step done.
Completed checks in the step list reflect persisted completion events, not steps viewed.
A dependent step can be previewed and marked done with an explicit override; the reader is never trapped.
A running timer's remaining time is reconstructed from its absolute deadline after reload, route change, or tab restore.
An elapsed timer is marked elapsed and neither the step nor the meal becomes complete.
Timer state changes and expiry are announced once across tabs, never every second.
Timers for other steps stay reachable in the tray.
Finishing offers batch confirmation, eating a serving, and finishing without bookkeeping as separate actions; nothing records intake automatically.
A recipe edit during cooking leaves the session on its original revision and says so.
Timer numerals stay whole and readable at large text sizes and 200 % zoom.
Mark step done, Previous, Next, timer controls, the step list, and Exit cooking are keyboard reachable.
With reduced motion, step changes and timer updates use no sliding or animated steam; changes are instant or brief fades.
The page never scrolls sideways at any supported viewport.
Light and Evening change palette and artwork only; the recipe, servings, dates, occurrences, layout, and actions are identical.
